title: External Application Head-Requirement Binding and Decision-Margin Qualification Closeout

scientific_finding.interpretation: The NSW Aquifer Interference Policy provides a genuine external decision-margin structure: near-threshold exceedance may be judged against the accuracy of an otherwise robust model. However, the policy does not prescribe a transferable numerical prediction-accuracy value. IESC uncertainty guidance independently confirms that acceptable prediction error and risk are quantity-of-interest, project and decision specific. Therefore the physical threshold magnitude cannot be reused as H_app.

rejected_substitutions: 0.2 m or 2 m physical drawdown threshold as H_app
calibration RMSE or normalised RMSE as prediction accuracy
MODFLOW or Richards solver convergence tolerance as application accuracy
F-GC07 observed coupling error as H_app or A_temporal
mass imbalance as an accuracy allocation

architecture_result.required_contract: A concrete application supplies a versioned numerical prediction-accuracy or decision-margin requirement with provenance, quantity of interest, receptor/location, time horizon and uncertainty semantics.
architecture_result.GC07_composition_role: F-GC07 supplies temporal/coupling numerical characterization and estimator signals. Those signals may be evaluated only after the external application contract supplies an admissible temporal allocation or equivalent numerical-error budget.

downstream.purpose: Materialize the versioned external application-accuracy contract and its composition seam without selecting a universal number. A concrete project can later instantiate that contract and qualify a numeric budget.
